name: Gridline Last-Mile Courier Weathershell
description: Issued to Gridline couriers operating across all weather conditions in M88's layered urban environment, this weathershell jacket does the heavy lifting of keeping drivers functional during twelve-hour shifts in rain, industrial particulate, and temperature swings across the city's climate-uneven districts. The outer shell is a seam-sealed ripstop with a hydrophobic coating that sheds water and light chemical spray. GPS antenna filaments are woven into the left sleeve, feeding route data directly to a wrist-mounted display or BCI interface. High-visibility orange panels at the shoulders and lower back are retroreflective. A rear hem vent accommodates tail modifications. The Gridline logo and courier ID number are printed on the back in weatherproof ink that remains scannable after heavy wear.
cultural_context: Gridline couriers are the circulatory system of M88's middle tiers — present everywhere, noticed by almost no one. The weathershell is practical enough that off-market versions are popular with people who need to move through the city without drawing attention. The courier ID on the back makes real Gridline shells risky to wear off-shift in some contexts.
story_hooks: A Gridline courier's GPS log shows they made a delivery to a location that officially doesn't exist — and they disappeared the same shift.
Someone is running a shadow courier network using stolen Gridline weathershells, exploiting the scanner-readable ID system to pass through corporate checkpoints.
The GPS filaments in a specific batch of weathershells have been compromised to transmit courier locations to a third party in real time.
